summary: Sheikh Ali Mashhour continues his discussion on Zadul-Ma'ad (Provisions for the Hereafter), focusing on things that open the heart to the Quran and divine guidance. The lecture emphasizes that true faith (iman) is a union of a pure heart with the revelation of Allah and His Sunnah. The sheikh explains that tawheed (Islamic monotheism) is foundational to all acts of worship, and without it, even good deeds have no value in the Hereafter. He illustrates this through examples such as the charity of non-believers and the necessity of wudu for valid prayer. The lecture extensively discusses various forms of shirk (polytheism/idolatry) in contemporary culture, including talismans, charms, lucky symbols, horoscopes, and fortune cookies, emphasizing that even Prophet Ibrahim remained vigilant against these practices throughout his life.
suggested_title: Tawheed as the Foundation of Worship: Identifying Modern Forms of Shirk
catchy_title: Why Did the Prophet Reject a Man's Hand?
